I've got more time in on PS4 but I wanted to quickly get this review up.

If you've played the previous entires then you know what you're in for here. This is a less than perfect MX simulator and it's far from a triple A game. However, having said that, this is the best entry into the series so far. There have been a lot of improvements over MXGP 3 and ME SX. The game has been copping some flak for the punishing ways in which your rider loses control of the bike, the tail sliding out excessively & frequently and the same old (well, worse) scrubs. Yes, those are all issues, but come on, we know what we're gonna get with a Milestone game. 
It's gonna be many years before we can call this series a true motocross sim, but this is not a bad game by any means and I'm sure the more serious issues will be patched.

The rider physics have been drastically improved and are inching their way closer to being realistic. The bike physics look genuinely good now as well. The AI are more difficult now but they still take the same lines and are predictable in every race. There's more variety this time around though, you'll see riders going off track and miscalculating their scrubs more often. 

The game looks great, the rain looks great (gone is that green rain from GP3), lighting is beautiful and the bikes are more detailed than ever before. It also looks much more real than previous entries, gone is the cartoony feel. 
The tracks have been rendered & scaled properly, the jumps, bumps, berms all look and feel the way they do in real life, which is something we haven't seen yet.  Wet tracks feel more realistic and are easier to race on now. Still though, ruts have no real impact and some of the corners are hard to take without sliding out when really there should be ruts that have developed to help. 

As for sound, the bikes sound better but still not amazing. The atmosphere sounds are pretty awful, the crowd cheering samples sound like they're coming from inside a stadium and not outdoors, same with the PA sound effects. The crowd still only cheer when your rider scrubs, and nobody else's, which is ridiculous. Besides the sounds of the bike though, this is all pretty irrelevant. 

Other minor improvements have been added as well, such as riders becoming transparent when they are immediately behind you in third person view, instead of blocking your screen (but if they've become transparent in game and you go to free cam, they'll be transparent there too, come on Milestone..). 

If you're a fan of the series or MX in general, picking this up should be a no brainer, just don't expect a perfect, polished game. 
7/10 for what it is.

I have played all the Milestone motorcycle games and with no doubt I must say that its the moste mature, best polished and most enjoyable their game to this date. Still its not without things I dislike but I can truly recomend it. 

Honestly I have never been riding on a MX bike but finally in this game physics are good, challenging, and it needs time to understand how to handle the bike. Front tire still has way too much grip (I really dont understand why Milestone is always making so unrealistic front tire grip) but finally in some situations you can flip the bike over or lowside.  Riding is not about stupid full throttle, its easy to loose rear grip or fall. Rigs and track line are very important. 

Finally bike set iu is nicely made and proper bike set up give advantage.  Like in MXGP 3 or MSX the graphics are fantastic (but still blurry), better animation, fantastic mud effect ant track deformation...but...still the rain look weird (not as bad as MXGP3). Unfortunately to fully enjoy you need very strong pc as I was able to play MXGP3 @60 FPS with full settings, now I hardly ever get 40fps. 

Its a big shame that if you bought MXGP3  you will fell that this game is "just" very upgraded version, but finally Milestone released a good game I really find it hard to complain about anything. Of course there are things that should be upgraded/added and despite writing about it many times it wasn't implemented. So again, my suggestions are: 
-more realistic front tire grip
-changable Field Of View for onboard camreas
-dynamic onboard camera allowing to look into apex or head movement depending on the rider lean
-compound riding in multiplyer mode
-sharp filter for graphics options

In short version: 
PROS:
-good, challanging physics (but yet too much grip for front tire)
-beautiful graphics, animations, track deformations
-enjoyable gameplay 
-nice career mode with extreme option
-big customisation
-working set up of the bike
-traning mode with echievements
-fantastic compound
-great sounds

CONS:
-very strong pc needed to use full gfx settings
-too much front tire grip
-annoying respawn when leaving track limits, in some cases instant respawn. 
-too short respawn time after crash
-no compound in multiplayer mode.

Of MXGP3, Monster Energy SX FIM 1, and this, MXGP PRO takes the cake for "realism."
You MUST straighten your scrubs out ELSE YOU WILL HI SIDE!!! This is what would actually happen, so using scrubs as a mid-long length AND changing directions jumping technique works well - the shorts straights better be straightened out or you are going down.
This title is the equivalent of Monster Energy SX 1 in terms of scope, sounds and feel in a GP package. The Compound has a seriously lacking SX but great MX and the  VAST offroad loops and figure 8 are great little nuances and OBVIOUSLY these devs are hinting at GNCC racing.... 
Theres a LOT to love here for 5.99 USD on sale....

You can set the Physics to easy, you can have auto lean enabled and even have unlimited rewinds if you make a mistake. This allows you to start easy and slowly increase the difficulty as you go, and you can make these adjustments between events during your career catering to your needs.
I find this game extremely satisfying to play and will continue to practice my skills till i can win a race with all the setting on max difficulty.

TL;DR: Overall, I am loving the game so far. It has flaws and hopefully sees some post launch support but its my favorite modern MX game.

I see a lot of negative reviews and while the game deserves critisism I think a lot of it is exagurated and people are giving impressions on a stock bike without doing the rider training. NOTE: Do the rider training! I didnt realize it was worth doing but it improves your rider in a number of ways which is a bit silly to hide that fact.

Ill address the common complaints and throw in my $.02

-Performance/graphics: I'm running a modern i5, SSD, 16gb RAM and 970 GTX. At 1080p with everything on max except bloom and motion blur I get a solid 60 fps on most tracks and 50 in the compound. I do not get the stuttering that it seems some people are getting, maybe I'm just lucky. The game looks great. Seeing the "ruts" fill up with water is pretty cool although it is a bit overdone and looks like you are just riding in a river by the end of the race. There is a distinct lack of water effects from riding through it on the track but its not nearly as bad as MX vs ATV All Out. My main complaint for the graphics is your back tire. It doesn't really appear to spin or change speeds apart from going and stop. There is particle effects kicked up from other bikes but your back tire appears lifeless

-AI: Is pretty mindless. They have one line in which they take and that is pretty well the extent of it. If you are in the way of that line they will crash into you

-Ruts and berms: The track deformation does affect gameplay however not really in a way I had hoped. The track gets beat up but really all it does is make it rougher and easier to go down but true ruts are never formed. However, even if they were, you would just slide out of them which leads into:

-Handling: I really enjoy the handling of the game (have only played on PRO). If you have played previous MXGP games you have a pretty good idea of what you are getting into. The back end slides out a bit more than I feel it should but its not nearly as bad as people are making it out to be. Again, put some better tires on your bike, do the training and its entirely different from when you first start up the game. You need to feather the throttle a bit to keep traction coming out of turns.

As far as the crashing on overjumps I see a lot of people saying its overdone however when I have watched gameplay of people complaining about it they are usually landing hard on their back wheel and wondering why they crash. I have crashed on a couple overjumps I felt as though I shouldn't have, used rewind and made sure I landed proper and rode away without a crash. No issue from me here.

My main complaint is the berms and how far over you can lean the bike before crashing. Some tracks have a hard, sharp berm on the outside corner. You should be able to lean the bike over and rail the corner. Instead you will either just blow over the top edge or crash from leaning over too hard. Apart from that I really enjoy the handling of the bikes.

Air Control: Again, do the training, it improves your air control and scrubs. Whips and scrubs, pretty well same as all the other MXGP games but a little bit better. Free in the sense that you can go as far as you want with them but not free like MX vs ATV games. The scrubs work pretty good to keep you low if you carve the face of the jump right but it wont let you do a Bubba scrub due to crashing from leaning over too hard. The air control is still fairly stiff but I feel as though its better than any previous MXGP games (note: I didnt play 3). I don't care about whips so I do not mind the air control although it could be improved

Sound: You're best off just watching a couple youtube videos if you are picky about the sound. Its passable to me.

Tracks: Same affair as previous games. Youre getting licenced tracks for better or worse. Personally, I don't like a lot of the tracks and I am hoping for some more North American style tracks down the road. The compound is pretty good.

Customization: Its gonna be a grind if you want to spruce up you're bike and rider. I don't really care about much of that apart from throwing the best components on my bike but there seems to be a pretty good deal of options to choose from if thats your thing.

[i]Small caveat: I received this game for free quite some time ago, much closer to release. However, due to having a video card that wasn't anywhere close to the recommended, I felt it necessary to wait until I had a better card to give the game a proper 'shake'. I've done as such, and these are their stories:

* Law and Order sound * [/i]

[b]MXGP Pro[/b] is the first game that I've played in the MXGP series since the very first. Now, I realize many compare this to MXGP3 but I have not played that and simply cannot compare.

[h1]Okay, so how are the physics?[/h1]
Well, they're pretty good. Mostly. 

The actual riding on dirt, at least hard pack and sand feels really good. Wet mud... less so. But the real kicker is that, even if you set the rider weight to manual, the others riders can push your rear wheel around and the bike will stay balanced like some sort of airbender riding a ball.  Additionally, if you land on another rider off a ramp, you'll land on a giant invisible hit box. Then slide off back onto the track. Now, all that seems kind of terrible. It's not the best. But, provided you stay on the track and not land on anyone, riding is quite enjoyable and relatively realistic. Terrain deformation is more prudent here. As the race goes on, the tracks will become more deformed and staying in the 'trenches' becomes a valuable guide of sorts. Having been compacted, it makes you go a lot faster. The bikes also feel appropriately heavy. 

There is a fairly robust [b]career[/b] mode. And you are able to adjust a number of settings in and out of the career. How much the AI does or does not control shifting the rider weight, gear ratio mapping, distance between the wheels, and much more. Some of these settings will affect the multiplier when awarded MX credits. Beyond the control scheme settings that affect MX credits, you'll also be able to choose how long each race is in each location. Whether you partake in the qualifiers or not and the difficulty of the other drivers. 

On top of these more personal settings. Winning races also nets you “fame”, I put it in quotes because it behaves as more of a currency if not a status. You don't spend it like MX credits, but it does get you things. Upon reaching certain fame levels, new sponsors will unlock. In turn, they'll give you parts that can also affect your bike's specs. They'll also provide specific tasks that, if performed, will get you more fame and MX credits. However, performing poorly can often lower your fame and lose the sponsorship. Typically, the sponsor objectives are things like placing above a spot in a GP, getting the 'holeshot', leading for X number of laps or performing a number 'scrubs'. MX credits allow you to buy cosmetic items for the rider. Stuff for the bike is restricted to sponsorship. There is also a lite pseudo social media mechanic where you can respond to other riders “tweets” which can start rivalries and also earn you more fame. 

[h1]Do you even scrub, bro?[/h1]
I honestly don't watch much MX stuff in real life. Maybe on a lazy Sunday. But I always wondered why the riders threw their tail out over jumps. I thought they were just showing off. Turns out, it's a technique to cut height off a jump without slowing down. And this game has a tutorial for it if the concept is rather new to you. 

Besides the career mode, there are quick races, championships and grands prix. However, if you back out of the main menu. You'll be able to free ride around a training ground. Hearkens back to the days when I'd ride around aimlessly in ATV Offroad Fury while playing Denial by Sevendust on repeat. 

[b][i]THE GIST:
MXGP Pro is a decent dirt bike sim racer. Personally, I find it overpriced. But, this is an issue that Milestone S.r.l. has had in the past. And to be honest, that paradigm is unlikely to change. I do recommend it on a sale, though.[/i][/b]

[h1] Introduction [/h1]

This is and in [b] Depth Review for MXGP Pro [/b]. If you don't want/have the time to read this just ignore the post. If you like it please leave a thumbs up and helpful!

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

The Gameplay of MXGP Pro is [b] smooth and easy to understand [/b] with the help of the tutorials and you will learn how to play the game in no time. If you have never played a MX Bike Racing game before start with a low difficulty and turn it higher after every race until you find a difficulty level that suits your skill. I recommend starting with Semi-Pro Physics and switching to Pro when you feel comfortable to do so.

[h1] Career [/h1]

The [b] Career Mode [/b] is nice but it is lacking a few features like fuel consumption for example. Before a Race Weekend the game let's you choose what sessions you want to play (Qualifying, Qualifying Race, Race 1 and Race 2), after choosing the lenght of the Weekend you will start in the box setting up your Bike settings (gearing, throttle and brake response, ecc...). The setup of the Bike is easy to understand and learn.

The qualifying sessions are just like in the real races. You have 25 Minutes to make a good time.
After the qualifying there is the race, you start in grid at the position you qualified, from now on it's self explanatory, just give it all you can to Win the Race!

In the [b] MotoGP™20 Career Mode [/b] you can will start in the MX2 Class (125 2-stroke and 250 4-stroke). You will have to choose a Team to ride for with your fame points (at the beginning you will ride for a smaller team, the more fame points you make, the better teams will be available for you to choose. After choosing a Team you will be able to decide which Bike you want to ride for the season and you will also be able to change the look of the bike (colors, mods and livery). The Career Mode of MXGP Pro is very well made and a step up from the previous game. It's a lot of fun and quite realistic!

[h1] Graphics [/h1]

The Graphics on MXGP Pro are [b] fine [/b], nothing too special, but still nice to see because of the motion blur which gives it a more cinematic feel and look. The textures and bikes models are flawless, the sky and track details are good, the Motion Blur is enough and not annoying (you can setup how much you want), the Game is also well optimized so you will also be able to run it on lower end PC's. The Movement of the Bike and the Rider look pretty realistic and smooth, there are some minor bugs with the Rider's movement but they rarely happen.

[h1] Audio [/h1]

The Audio of MXGP Pro is fine, the only bummer is the 2-Strokes and the lack of power and aggressivity in the Sound of the Bikes, which makes it less realistic. But we all know that's hard to do.

[h1] Difficulty [/h1]

If you have never played a MX Bike Racing Game before you will take some time to get used to the racing lines, braking and bike movement whilst braking. After getting used to it, it's just a matter of getting faster and faster on Track and improving the feeling and safety (crashing less). I found it that not having played a MX Racing game before, after around 40 Hours I am feeling good at Max Difficulty (realistic), being able to fight for the win on tracks where my feeling is good after the practice, and for the Top 5 where the it's not. BE Hard to yourself when setting up the difficulty of the Game, this gives you a challange and makes the game fun and hard!

[h1] Multiplayer [/h1]

The [b] Multiplayer [/b] is pretty much dead so you will have to play with friends in that case.

[h1] Game Time [/h1]

To complete a Career it takes time (19 Grand Prix's), and to win MX2 and MXGP it is goind to be many hours you will spend on this Game, so be ready to play this game for a long time if you are looking for these results and good deals from good teams.

[h1] Price [/h1]

I bought this Game during a sale for 15€ and it was well worth it! I am guessing a good price for this game to buy it would be around 25€ during non-sale periods.

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

I am happy with this Game, it is a lot of fun if you are a fan of [b] MXGP and MX2. [/b] I give this Game and [b] 7.5 out for 10 [/b] with the only negative points being that it's very time consuming and the sound lacking in development and there are a lot of nice features missing, that they could add for realism and fun. I hope my in-depth review helped you to choose if you want to buy the game or not! :)

[h1]Hands Down The Best Motocross Game To Date.[/h1]
I've played and enjoyed every MXGP game and enjoyed the crap out of MESX.
[i](..and yes I've also played MX simulator, which is also not realistic btw so stop saying that, but it is lots of fun)[/i]

With that being said this is by far my favorite handling so far, so many nice improvements from the previous games.

I can relate to why a lot of people are rating the game down though. The handling is much different then previous titles, I myself was at first put off by the new handling and even found myself getting frustrated, but after giving it some good time to learn and let it sink in it's now easy to control the bike and natural and now I absolutely love it and welcome the change.

I read one review that stated it's handling is the same as MESX, that is simply not true, it is much different.

[h1]Major Improvements:[/h1] 
+Throttle Control: The biggest improvement which I believe is the cause of many negative comments on the game is that you now need to modulate the throttle for the turns. Turning sharp with full throttle is going to slide you out into a crash and I love this! To me it actually gives the bikes a feeling of having a bit more power to them which I felt was lacking in previous iterations. If you let off the throttle, brake/ turn, shift your weight right, you will be just fine ;)

+Landing Jumps: Landing your jumps correctly is now vastly more important than the previous titles, cased jumps or a big jump that bottoms out your suspension is going to cause you to crash, this was needed so badly. Sure on multiplayer if you weren't  landing the jumps right it would cause you to lose the race but the feeling of how much it matters was never fully there before and because of this a few sections were actually faster to not do them correctly.  

+Tracks: Compared to MXGP 3 the tracks just feel much more lively to me, much better jumps and the look and feel of the terrain is over all much better, way less flat lots of little details and uneveness.

[h1]Nuetral:[/h1]

-Terrain deformation It's there but minimal, don't expect deep ruts or anything forming on turns in the wet, after a lot of laps the tracks will just seem a bit more slippery and on straights riding where others have will feel slightly more smooth. Stilll cool to be able to see where everyone has ridden though.

-The snap-on to berm physics which made riding around a berm in MESX a breeze (albeit a bit strange to notice it snapping to it) is now gone. Have not decided yet if this is good or a bad change.

-The whips: doesn't really affect racing but I'll agree not the best.

-Still no female riders

[h1]Negative[/h1]

AI: I know a lot of people are saying the AI is much harder but once you get used to the game and get good with an upgraded bike.. the ai is still too easy which has been the plague of every MXGP game so far. I think a lot of people just forget what it was like to race starting out in the other games before their bike was upgraded, and before they knew the tracks.

--No Level Editor, so stuck with the tracks they give us. Which are fantastically made but limited in quantity 


[h1]Additional[/h1]
++: I play in exclusively in first person, so all impressions are from that point of view. Milestone has really nailed the first person camera in their games. The way it feels and looks is so natural.

Tip: You know that rewind thing (the thing that you never use because it feels like cheating and you feel like a noob using it)? Try using it in this one at first, but specifically as a learning tool, it will help you greatly in learning the new handling then turn it off once you got the hang of it.

First off, let me start by saying that I am a hard person to please when it comes to MX/SX games. These games are my way to get a taste of racing after I got hurt and couldn't ride anymore... Like many people, I have been waiting for a game that not only provides the mechanics, physics, licensed products, etc.- but also the things that aren't usually focused on by these developers: exciting racing. Milestone has given me hope that this dream game will exist- sooner than later.

The usual MX game experience:
1) Ride a stock Chinabike while wearing ugly gear
2) Think to yourself "great- another floaty turd of a game"
3) Unlock some steezy threads
4) Grind the career to unlock tracks and a 450
5) Finish said career
6) Buy DLC name-brand bike(s)
7) Rinse and repeat
8) Do this all until you get bored of it and go back to a FPS shooter

This game does not provide any of that garbage. The new physics and features of this game add an excitment that I haven't had playing a motocross game since Reflex. What separates this game from the previous releases? The extreme career, paired with the improved physics and deformation (IMO). It's been a long time since I've raced, but I think that Milestone has done a really great job making the game as realistic as possible- without being impossible to make it through a race without biting the dirt. For once, I haven't won every race (unless I restart multiple times)- which is a welcomed improvement over past Milestone games (where you literally cannot lose to the AI unless you suck).

There is still much to do on the side of realism and the career (where did our official team sponsorships go Milestone?), which is lacking compared to previous MXGP games. I would also like to see:

- Popular MX fonts to customize our jerseys and number plates (so that we can look as cool as the official riders)
- Offical team rides (like there used to be in MXGP games)
- The ability to have sponsor's logos on your gear
- Further improvements to the new physics system (mainly ruts and deformation)
- Fix random crashes, incorrect timing/scoring/results
- Make the game not crash when I try to select a Yamaha 450 in career mode (literally cannot select this bike without the game crashing immediately)
- Improving the features added to this title- they're all great additions to these games!

All in all- I highly recommend this game. It's the best MX game (IMO) to date. Can't wait until the next SX game!!!

Two good steps forward, one big step back for this franchise.

I'm enjoying the more challenging cornering and ground physics. It really shines on rougher tracks where finesse is key to maintaining good speed and fast lines. I also really appreciate a more open tuning system to get your bike setup the way you like it, and tune your bike for your lines at different tracks and surfaces. These feel like really awesome improvements to the gameplay.

I really love the choppy rutty tracks in this game with these 'pro' physics setup. It takes way more finesse and control, and feels awesome. I've noticed in longer races, the deformation eventually just flattens out the lines, rather than make them choppy or blown out. I get why this works this way, but it would be cool if lines got rougher and harder over time, rather than smoother. This is really apparently in long motos, where the A.I leaves a 5 foot wide perfectly flat race line through the whole track, which brings me to my next point.

The AI seems largely unchanged and is as slow and one lined as any of their other games. They simply follow the same path around the track lap after lap, never changing lines and providing only a challenge for the first few motos while you get comfortable with a setup. After I found a good base setting in my second ever moto, I've been easily 2-5+ seconds a lap faster than the A.I, which is hugely dissapointing. By my estimation, Milestone expected the increased riding difficulty meant the A.I is inherently more challenging. It works to a degree, and I think they're probably on to something with that formula. If the A.I took different and varying lines, which made the track rougher and more difficult over time, riding smoothly and fast would be more challening, making the whole game much harder and more fun/realistic.

The most maddening step backwards is the in air controls. The scrub and whip, apparently 'helped by' Tim Gajser is the absolute wost it's been yet. Gajser, while an amazing rider; is apparently a very poor gameplay designer. I am mostly shocked that they took such a huge step backwards on a feature seemed to be improving all too slowly. There is no longer any 'feel' in trying to lean off a jump, it doesn't matter how fast or slow you move the control sticks, the rider simple snaps the bike sideways in which you have to counter steer back to land safely. It's absolutely madenning how bad this is, at least in MXGP3/MES you can control the speed and amount of english you put on the bike. Why are you struggling so hard with this Milestone? I just don't understand after all these years of being dragged kicked and screaming to adding more control and feel, you've now completely gone backwards again. It just doesn't make any sense whatsoever.

Graphics are great, sound is great. They're continuing to up the fidelity and it all looks and sounds awesome. The career mode and sponsor stuff is all fine and pretty good so far. It also runs great on my iMac with bootcamp. I'm really bummed there is still no FOV adjustment for those of us who primarily ride in first person.

Overall it's a fun game, and a welcome installment. I just wish the A.I could go as fast paced as Milestone does at releasing these games.

Here we have the best MXGP game so far, but "Pro" physics are a joke, all "Pro" changes is the game will eject you right off of your bike for [what Milestone considers] the slightest over-jump. LOL!

"Semi-pro" is the good old MXGP physics without the BS. Most of the major reviewers are much too egotistical to even try "semi-pro" physics (because they are SOOoooo pro, you know) thus most of the negative reviews - including Youtube - reflect the opinions formed around the garbage "Pro" physics. Just save yourself ALL the hassle. Semi-pro physics are *exactly* the same as Pro physics without the awesome experience of being ejected off of your bike constantly for trying to land jumps that these riders easily land in real life, no problem.

No matter the physics setting (standard/semi-pro/pro), ruts and berms do not have the overpowered electromagnetic attraction that was so apparent in MXGP 3. You have to go almost too slow to hook a berm, and finding and catching ruts is a fools errand. Milestone needs to find a balance between the gravitational pull of the sun that was berms and ruts in MXGP 3, and the weak sauce that is ruts and berms in MXGP Pro.

Traction is less than past MXGP games, yet grip was too high before. Here you will need a semblance of throttle control wherein past games you could quite literally pin the throttle almost the entire time.
Again, FIND THE BALANCE, Milestone...

Whips and scrubs have never been better, and honestly anyone that complains is a newb (that probably hasn't completed the "tutorial" and unlocked better whip/scrub "technique") and should just shut up. They are better in this game than even Monster Energy Supercross (and MESX2), and certainly better than previous MXGP games.

Graphics have been improved tremendously, rain isn't absolutely terrible looking anymore, reflections are great. Animations are much better now.

You can no longer cheese the starting gate for guaranteed holeshots, and beyond that there are many more small and sometimes subtle improvements, which I won't get into here but if you are an MXGP fan you will notice them and appreciate them.

Bloom appears to be broken on Qatar/Losail, so if your FPS and performance tanks on that track, disable the bloom effect and re-enable it once you complete your races there.

Contrary to almost anything you'll read or hear about it, terrain deformation does in fact exist here, and it's pretty decent actually. However, as mentioned previously in regards to ruts and berms, it doesn't actually affect much...other than making you crash more often if you play with Pro physics. Ha...ha...

On the surface, MXGP Pro seems like a solid step forward for milestone's series of dirtbike games. The fourth MXGP title boasts a much improved physics system, and track deformation graphical enhancements. First, lets dive into the all-new Pro physics.

In my mind, Milestone has always created the most enjoyable and challenging riding experience when it comes to physics, but it had some major issues that needed addressed. Many were, here with Pro physics. Gone are the days of casing a jump, or drifting through a corner at ludicris speeds. Pro physics require attention to detail at every level, from speed, cornering angle, power input, jump takeoffs and landings, braking, and put it all together in order to make successful laps. For me, this makes even Milestone's latest release, MESX, unplayable. That's impressive. 

Another welcome improvement is track deformation. Simply put, it's some of the best I've seen in a dirtbike game, and defintitely the best Milestione has produced. Hopefully it's here to stay.

The compound is back, and more beautiful than ever. Although, that does come with it's issues. While most of the game performs outstandingly well on my 6th gen i7 and Nvidia GTX1080 (1440p @ >100fps) the compound has some severe stuttering and frame rate drops. Fortunately, I don't spend much time there anyway, but if that's your thing, be aware of this issues. Within compound mode, you can compete in MX or SX races or time trials.

The menues and ui have not been improved whatsoever, and in fact, are worse off than in MESX. Some major issues still remain, for example, when selecting your number, you still cannot manually select it. You still have to scroll through 900 and some numbers, which is obviously frustrating (especially just after you buy the game and are excited to get racing). There also is a bug with the tv camera in replay. Some players have mentioned it's just after certain motos, however, whenever I have tried to use the replay, tv camera has not worked for me. Also, when backing out of replay, the screen and sound freeze for about 10-15 seconds before resuming. Asthetically, I personally find the ui a bit dated looking and unattractive. 

The sound is gernerally underwhelming, as per usual. The commentary is corny and adds to the dated and childish feel of the ui to start the events. The bikes don't sound bad, but I don't feel immersed in the race due to poor sound engineering and mixing. The general atmosphere is also not captured, and theres alot of issues with dynamic track events, such as running through water, but I'll get to that. Overall, the sound isn't bad, but I do notice it taking me out of the experience sometimes, which obviously isn't good. 

Multiplayer currently has two options: quick match and create a match. So far, I have not seen a way to browse games like you could in MESX. Another missing feature from MESX in multiplayer, is the ability to vote on weather conditions for the race after voting for the track. That was a great feature that should have been implemented into MXGP Pro. So far I've had a great experience racing in multiplayer, especially when locking the physics to pro. 

Career mode is back and only has a couple differences from previous versions. A new fame rating has been added, which affects which sponsors you may choose. Your main sponsor determines your livery. Again, there are no factory teams available. Fame also dictates what brand/level parts you may install on your bike. These act as secondary sponsors. Each sponsor will have a goal for you to perform at each event. The completion of these goals reward you with credits and fame. Credits may be spent on outfit parts. This is career mode. Yay.

I think there is alot of room to grow in career mode. It'd be great to see drivers have ratings on different riding skills, the way many  other sports games give ratings to players in different skill categories. It'd be great to start off as a low level in skills such as "balance", "cornering", "starts", "jumps (takeoff and landings)", "agressiveness (affects ability to stay on bike when making contact with another rider)", "toughness (affects ability to stay on bike when another rider makes contact with you)", "stamina (affects all abilities over duration)", "whoops", etc. This would add a great level of gameplay and replayability to the series and could even bleed over into sponsors looking for riders with certain skills above a certain level. It'd also be nice to see contracts added into career mode as well. (And factory teams)!!

Other single player modes include, Grand Prix single races, Championship, etc. The usual. 

So overall we have pretty much what we are used to with a couple of really great upgrades. But is this good enough? 

No.

You still can't change the camera view before the race starts and it still resets to the default third person camera. Why?

The upgraded physics are awesome, and were necessary. But they are a wasted effort when the tracks lack dynamic physical properties. Sure, they look great, with ruts, deformation, water when it rains, etc, but none of that translates to the bike, or even the rest of the environment. The bike reacts only to the surface type and inclination/elevation of the track, and very (very, very) few scripted ruts and puddles. You feel the surface you are supposed to be racing on very well, but not the track you ARE racing on. This is a huge and experience ruining problem. You skate over any and all ruts that aren't huge and explicitly placed in the track by the devs. Again, not dynamic. If you hit one of the puddles, you hear it....but if it's raining and the whole track is covered in water? You aren't really driving through water. Theres no sound of water. Theres no splash of water. Theres no resistance on your bike as if driving through a massive trench of water or any other affect on your bike for that matter, be it grip or what have you. There's also no splash animation for water, or any being thrown up by tires. In fact theres not really much dirt, dust, or any of that thrown up but tires whiles accellerating, skidding, landing, etc. Of course my next suggestion couldn't happen until all that stuff does, because it'd be totally unbelievable, but wouldn't it be cool to have some dirt, water, dust, etc on your camera, or goggles, while you're racing. I see AI ripping off tear offs during races and I think, "yeah right". 

Speaking of AI, it still sucks. 

Overall, the issues ruin the experience. If you want to check out the new physics, wait for a sale. 5/10
